doc.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]

title: Inequality, sports pay and the Depression
summary: Budd on rich and poor, athletes' salaries, and remembering 1929.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Almost, yeah. So I’m doing the dream job here you know, going around interviewing all my heroes.
Well it’s a job that, there’s no other you’d rather have.
No, I’m sure you wouldn’t. But you’ve a long time to go. And you’re going to see things happen. I hope they’re going to get better and better.
Well there’s inequality in the music business.

Oh in everything. There’s some basketball players that are making more money than the president of the United States. More than executives in big companies. And it’s unequal. The poor are getting poorer, and the rich are getting richer. There’s an old song in my day, “Ain’t We Got Fun.” And one of the punch lines, The rich get rich and the poor get children/Ain’t we got fun. That was one of the lines. That’s in the days like “Brother Can You Spare A Dime” were popular, and that really had a meaning for people, didn’t it?

And when I talk about it now I’ve heard them say oh the depression back there in 1977, and 1982 was pretty bad. Was nothing to me. I saw 1929 when the banks were closed for three or four days. You should have somebody to evict people.
